title: Focused history and exam
description: Sets pre-test probability and picks the hypotheses to chase.

title: 12-lead ECG
description: Best initial test; triggers the emergency pathway when ischemic.

title: Chest radiograph
description: Class 1 recommendation to look for other cardiac, pulmonary and thoracic causes.

title: Serial high-sensitivity troponin and risk class
description: Feeds the clinical decision pathway (low, intermediate, high risk).

title: Pre-test scoring of what is left
timing: In parallel, for open must-not-miss causes
description: A validated score sets the probability band that selects the next test.

title: D-dimer
timing: Only at low or intermediate probability
description: Rule-out blood test; never confirms.

title: Definitive imaging for what remains
description: Settles what earlier steps could not.

title: If the dangerous causes are eliminated
description: Noncardiac causes become the working diagnosis.

title: History and exam
description: Sets which causes are plausible.

title: 12-lead ECG
description: Screens for ischemia.

title: Chest radiograph
description: Finds lung causes and changes PE probability.

title: Natriuretic peptide
timing: Single measurement in new suspected heart failure
description: Rule-out test for heart failure.

title: PE route
timing: In parallel if PE is open
description: Wells or PERC, then D-dimer or CTPA (see chest pain).

title: Echocardiography
timing: If heart failure is not ruled out
description: Confirms the cardiac abnormality.

title: History and exam
description: Location and migration of pain narrow the list.

title: Pregnancy test
timing: Before imaging, in anyone who could be pregnant
description: Decides whether pregnancy causes are possible and which imaging is safe.

title: Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler
description: Transabdominal plus transvaginal ultrasound is the usual first imaging.

title: Contrast CT
timing: Nonpregnant adults with a suspected non-gynecologic cause
description: Most accurate test for appendicitis and other bowel causes.

title: Red-flag history (SNNOOP10)
description: Structured screen of every new or different headache.

title: Neurologic exam
description: Decides which rules can be used.

title: Ottawa SAH rule
timing: Alert patients, normal neuro exam, peak within 1 hour
description: Six features: age 40 or older, neck pain or stiffness, witnessed loss of consciousness, onset with exertion, thunderclap onset, limited neck flexion.

title: Noncontrast head CT
description: First imaging test for suspected SAH and before LP in at-risk patients.

title: Lumbar puncture or CT angiography
timing: If still at risk after a negative CT
description: Second-line test chosen with the patient.

title: If no red flags and secondary causes are excluded
description: Primary headache becomes the working diagnosis.

title: Screening tool
description: NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS rather than qSOFA alone (strong recommendation).

title: Grade the certainty
description: Definite, probable, possible or unlikely sepsis, using the guideline's standard language.

title: Time-limited investigation
description: Search for infection within a set time before committing to antimicrobials.

title: Blood lactate
description: Suggested in the 2021 edition; re-check against 2026.

title: Source search
description: Chest film; lumbar puncture when meningitis is suspected.

title: Event history
description: Separates low-risk reflex patterns from high-risk features.

title: Exam with lying and standing blood pressure
description: Part of the standard initial evaluation.

title: 12-lead ECG
description: Class I in the initial evaluation.

title: Risk stratification and disposition
description: Sorts patients into high, intermediate and low risk.

title: Targeted tests only when suspected
description: Routine labs, cardiac imaging and carotid imaging are not useful without a specific reason.

title: Risk score
description: Glasgow-Blatchford score.

title: Endoscopy
description: Finds and treats the source.

title: Pre-test probability (Wells for DVT)
description: Low, intermediate or high; DVT prevalence about 10% or less, 25% and 50% or more.

title: Highly sensitive D-dimer
description: Rule-out test.

title: Compression ultrasound
description: Proximal or whole-leg ultrasound.

title: Classify by timing and triggers
description: Decides which bedside test applies.

title: Dix-Hallpike test
description: Diagnoses posterior canal BPPV.

title: HINTS exam by a trained clinician
description: Separates central from peripheral patterns.

title: MRI
description: Confirmatory test.

title: Bedside glucose
description: Detects and urgently corrects severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia.

title: Brain imaging: noncontrast CT or MRI
description: Assesses ischemic burden and excludes hemorrhage before any reperfusion treatment (class 1, level A).

title: ECG and troponin
description: Recommended, but must not delay treatment.

title: Vascular and perfusion imaging
timing: Suspected large vessel occlusion within 24 hours; extended windows
description: CT/CTA or MRI/MRA as fast as possible for thrombectomy selection.

title: Red-flag history and exam
description: The cornerstone of initial assessment.

title: No imaging if no red flags
description: All imaging is rated usually not appropriate.

title: MRI
timing: Red flags, or no improvement after 6 weeks
description: Modality of choice for most patients who need imaging.

title: Noncontrast CT
description: Imaging study of choice.

title: Ultrasound
timing: Pregnancy, or to look for obstruction
description: First choice in pregnancy; less sensitive for stones.

title: Contrast CT or MRI
description: Second-line imaging.
